column3: a paren evaluates FIRST; the splice carries the scalar result
a string payload splices as itself
an atom payload splices as itself
…also via the paren spelling — the atom is the payload
none splices as itself
a boolean splices as itself
a map payload is ONE value — no element spreading for maps
the map's paren value evaluates before the splice wraps it

column1: # --- §2 def name word <value>: the marker binds, forward form only -----

column3: an explicit code splice runs against the live stack
a non-list marker binding splices the single value back
a map marker binding yields the map value at reference
an atom rides the marker unchanged
a paren payload was evaluated at def time — the splice re-plays 6

column1: def inc word [1 add] 5 inc inc
column3: code-splice chain: each replay sees the live stack

column1: def inc2 word [2 add] 0 inc2 inc2
column3: …and a two-token payload chains the same way
each reference re-splices the elements
inside a list literal both splices flatten — four elements
the splice fires INSIDE the paren before quote can mark it
quote captures the literal token `word`; the list evaluates apart
a code payload fires in the paren — dup meets an empty stack
holding a list stops the reference from splicing — s stays a raw word

column1: def s word [dup add] quote [s] size
column3: the held reference is one node, not the payload's two

column1: def s word [dup add] quote s
column3: quote captures the NAME of a splice-bound def, binding notwithstanding

column1: def n word 42 quote n eq n/q
column3: …and the captured name is an ordinary atom
a map VALUE position binds the payload list as a value — no spread
a map payload nests as a map value
a splice reference inside an if branch fires when the branch runs
…and never fires in the untaken branch
an empty splice vanishes inside a list literal
…splicing nothing into an empty literal leaves it empty
double reference doubles the elements
a scalar marker contributes one element per reference
a one-element payload lands as the container's element

column3: a def'd LIST body absorbs a splice reference at eval time

column3: a code splice replays inside a fn body against the frame stack

column1: def w word [1,2] quote [0 w 9] size
column3: held: the reference is one raw node between the literals

column1: # --- §5 /q atoms and the three quote spellings ---------------------------

column3: the suffix form parses straight to an atom
the function form captures the upcoming word
…and the paren form is the same capture, grouped
suffix and function form produce the SAME atom
quoting a BOUND name still yields the plain atom
a registered word quotes to its name — no dispatch
an atom's type
the function form types identically
an atom is NOT its spelling string
…conversion is the explicit bridge
different names, different atoms
same name orders equal
atoms order by name
…and the comparison words agree
atoms sort lexically by name
the bare type literal sorts below every concrete atom
an atom and a string share no ordering — use tcmp
atom-bearing lists compare structurally
the captured `true` atom is the ordinary atom true/q
an atom map value stays an atom
multiple atom-valued fields
an options-style atom flag reads back by dot access

column1: def o {mode: fast/q} o.mode eq fast/q
column3: …and dispatches on eq like any atom
atoms are plain elements in data lists
…and read back unevaluated (an atom never re-fires)
a /q atom inside a HELD list is one node
the paren spelling works in a map value slot
…but the bare function form does not — parenthesise it
an atom interpolates as its bare name

column1: # --- §7 auto-splice at reference: the marker vs the value ----------------

column3: marker binding: reference explodes to elements
value binding: reference is the one list
the spread makes a FLAT 3-element list — longer than the nested form
the container absorbs the spread
the value stays one element

column3: splices chain through other splices and flatten
value bindings nest instead
a scalar splice feeds the next word
…indistinguishable from a value binding for scalars
